parts.visual:
Blockbuster Video made billions renting DVDs. A tiny startup called Netflix offered streaming video. In 2005, streaming video was low-quality, blurry, and slow. Blockbuster's CEO laughed at it. 'Our customers want high-quality DVDs!' Five years later, internet speeds increased. Streaming became flawless. Blockbuster went bankrupt. Netflix became a monopoly.

The Dilemma:
1. The Innovator's Dilemma: A brilliant theory by Clayton Christensen. It explains why perfectly managed, highly profitable companies are constantly destroyed by cheap, ugly startup technology.
2. The Blind Spot: Giant companies listen to their best customers. Their best customers demand 'better, faster, more expensive' products. A startup builds something 'cheap, ugly, but convenient' for people who have no money. By the time the ugly technology improves and steals the rich customers, it is too late for the Giant to react.
parts.audio: Great companies do not fail because they are stupid. They fail because they do exactly what business school teaches them: they listen to their most profitable customers and ignore the cheap, low-margin experiments at the bottom of the market.

questions.question: What is a 'Sustaining Innovation' vs. a 'Disruptive Innovation'?
options: Sustaining innovation makes an existing product better for existing rich customers (e.g., a TV with slightly better colors). Disruptive innovation creates a completely new, usually cheaper and worse product, that unlocks a massive new market of people who couldn't afford the old product.
questions.correct_answer: Sustaining innovation makes an existing product better for existing rich customers (e.g., a TV with slightly better colors). Disruptive innovation creates a completely new, usually cheaper and worse product, that unlocks a massive new market of people who couldn't afford the old product.
questions.explanation: Disruption always starts at the bottom, looking like a toy.

questions.question: Listen to the Kodak executive in 1995 explaining why they ignored digital cameras. What was their fatal mistake?
questions.tts_text: We invented the digital camera in our labs! But the photos were incredibly blurry. And more importantly, we make 90% of our profits selling physical film chemicals. If we push digital cameras, we will destroy our own billion-dollar film business. We have to bury it.
options: The Fear of Cannibalization. A giant company will actively refuse to launch a new, disruptive technology if that new technology threatens to destroy their current, highly profitable business model. They choose short-term safety over long-term survival.
questions.correct_answer: The Fear of Cannibalization. A giant company will actively refuse to launch a new, disruptive technology if that new technology threatens to destroy their current, highly profitable business model. They choose short-term safety over long-term survival.
questions.explanation: If you don't cannibalize yourself, someone else will.

questions.question: Why do disruptive technologies usually look like 'Toys' when they first launch?
options: Because the technology is immature. The first personal computers couldn't do anything useful for a massive corporation; they were just toys for hobbyists in garages. Giants ignore them because toys don't generate $100 Million in corporate revenue.
Because they are painted bright colors.
questions.correct_answer: Because the technology is immature. The first personal computers couldn't do anything useful for a massive corporation; they were just toys for hobbyists in garages. Giants ignore them because toys don't generate $100 Million in corporate revenue.
questions.explanation: Never ignore the toy. The toy will grow up.

questions.question: How can a Giant company survive the Innovator's Dilemma?
options: The 'Skunkworks' Model. The CEO must create a completely separate, secret team in a different building, give them their own budget, and order them to build the exact product that will destroy the parent company. They must act like an independent startup.
questions.correct_answer: The 'Skunkworks' Model. The CEO must create a completely separate, secret team in a different building, give them their own budget, and order them to build the exact product that will destroy the parent company. They must act like an independent startup.
questions.explanation: You cannot fight a pirate if you are wearing a navy uniform.
